explanation: Apply F(n)=F(n−1)+F(n−2) recursively and cache computed values so repeated subproblems are reused. The cache persists across calls.
timeComplexity: O(n) expected work for a fresh query: n states, each with constant-time cache work. A previously cached query is O(1) expected. Iterative code makes n updates with two values; memoized code computes n states and retains them.
spaceComplexity: O(n_max) retained cache across calls, plus O(n) recursion for a fresh query. Iteration keeps two consecutive values. Memoized variants retain cached states and recursive frames.
attribution: Unmodified reference source: epi_judge_cpp_solutions/fibonacci.cc. Elements of Programming Interviews Judge authors; repository LICENSE: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 International. Explanation authored for EPI Practice.
correctness: The base cases return F(0)=0 and F(1)=1. Each new cached state adds two smaller correct states, so induction proves it equals F(n). Caching changes only reuse, not the recurrence.
walkthrough: For n=7, compute and cache F(2)=1, F(3)=2, F(4)=3, F(5)=5, F(6)=8 and F(7)=13; repeated requests for these states reuse their cached results. The walkthroughCase uses the judge’s JSON input format and expected observation.
edgeCases: n=0 and n=1 are recurrence bases.
For the fixed-width callable, require the requested Fibonacci value to fit its integer result.
The persistent cache may already contain results from earlier calls.
